relation_types.label: Contains vocabulary
relation_types.description: A sentence or transcript contains a vocabulary item.

relation_types.label: Uses grammar
relation_types.description: A sentence or vocabulary item uses or demonstrates a grammar pattern.

relation_types.label: Example of
relation_types.description: An item is an example of another language item or grammar concept.

relation_types.label: Source of
relation_types.description: A transcript, resource, or source item produced another item.

relation_types.label: Derived from
relation_types.description: An item was derived from another item.

relation_types.label: Opposite of
relation_types.description: Two items are direct opposites or antonyms.

relation_types.label: Contrast with
relation_types.description: Two items should be compared because they express contrasting meaning, usage, or logic.

relation_types.label: Confusable with
relation_types.description: Two items are easy to confuse and should be studied together.

relation_types.label: Negative counterpart
relation_types.description: A sentence or expression has a positive/negative counterpart.

relation_types.label: Translation of
relation_types.description: An item is a translation of another item.

relation_types.label: Translation variant of
relation_types.description: An item is an alternative translation or meaning variant.

relation_types.label: Formal variant of
relation_types.description: An item is a more formal variant of another item.

relation_types.label: Informal variant of
relation_types.description: An item is a more informal variant of another item.

relation_types.label: Slang variant of
relation_types.description: An item is a slang variant of another item.

relation_types.label: Register variant of
relation_types.description: An item differs by register, tone, formality, or context.

relation_types.label: Grammar contrast with
relation_types.description: Two grammar concepts should be compared because learners may confuse them.
